# How to write a drawcast (short rules)

A drawcast is a short teaching figure drawn on screen while a voice explains
it, like a short video. You write it as ONE JSON object. The player draws the
elements when the commands name them and speaks each `speak` line aloud.

## The story

- Open with the question the drawcast answers, said in the first spoken line.
- Then ONE concrete example with correct numbers, one change at a time.
- End on ONE insight, said in plain fresh words in the last line or two.
- 8 to 14 spoken lines. Each `speak` is one or two short sentences for the
  ear. Connect the sentences ("So…", "But…", "Now…"), do not list facts.
- No signposting ("Notice that", "Here we see"). Use $ for money unless the
  request uses another currency. Never invent a study, quote or statistic:
  use illustrative numbers and say so ("say a loan of $1,000…").

## The JSON object

```
{"title": "...",
 "domain": {"x": [0, 30], "y": [0, 8]},
 "vars": {"r": {"value": 0.05, "min": 0, "max": 0.1}},
 "elements": [ ... ],
 "commands": [ ... ]}
```

- `title`: a few words, shown under the player.
- `domain`: only when axes and curves use real units.
- `vars`: optional numbers that `animate` can change.
- `elements`, or `template` + `params` (see Templates), or both.

## Elements (each has a unique `id` and a `type`)

Ids: lowercase letters, digits and `_`, like `cost_line`. Never a lone
place or colour word (`left`, `top`, `red`).

- `{"id": "ax", "type": "axes", "x_label": "Years", "y_label": "Money"}`
- `{"id": "c1", "type": "curve", "expr": "(1+r)^x"}` — `expr` in x; may read vars.
- `{"id": "p1", "type": "point", "at": {"x": 10, "on": "c1"}}` — a point on a curve.
- `{"id": "l1", "type": "label", "attach_to": "c1", "side": "above", "text": "Compound"}`
  — a label ALWAYS has `attach_to` + `side` (above, below, left, right).
- `{"id": "n1", "type": "node", "text": "Seed"}` — a box with words.
- `{"id": "e1", "type": "edge", "from": {"ref": "n1"}, "to": {"ref": "n2"}}` — an arrow between nodes.
- `{"id": "chain", "type": "group", "members": ["n1", "n2", "n3"], "layout": "row"}`
  — boxes in a row/column/grid; the group places them. Never give boxes x/y.
- `{"id": "eq", "type": "math", "tex": "A = P(1+r)^t", "at": {"place": "top_right"}}`
  — a formula; it NEEDS an `at` (place: center, top, right, top_right, …).
  Never type a formula as plain text.
- `{"id": "pic", "type": "icon", "of": "apple", "size": 80}` — a picture of a thing.
- `{"id": "calc", "type": "scratch", "work": ["$1,000 × 1.05", "= $1,050"]}` —
  working, line by line; draw `calc_box` and `calc_line_1`, then `calc_line_2`…

Canvas words are cues: a word or three. The voice says the sentence. At most
about eight texts on the page. Leave out positions: the player places things.

Colours (only if needed, quoted): ink "#3d3833", two contrasted things
"#b5482e" (red) and "#2f6b8f" (blue), guides "#8f887c". Write them as
`"style": {"color": "#2f6b8f"}`; `"dash": true` in style for a dashed line.

## Commands (a list; ONE verb per command, `speak` on the same command)

- `{"card": {"title": "Why savings snowball"}}` — ALWAYS the first command.
- `{"draw": ["ax", "c1"], "speak": "..."}` — draws those ids, in order.
- `{"highlight": {"target": ["c1"]}, "speak": "..."}` — glows one thing.
- `{"point": {"at": {"ref": "p1"}, "gesture": "circle"}, "speak": "..."}`
  — gestures: circle, tap, underline.
- `{"animate": {"r": 0.07}, "duration": 3, "speak": "..."}` — changes a var
  (or a template param) smoothly; everything that reads it follows.
- `{"fade": {"target": ["c1"], "to": 0.25}}`, `{"erase": ["c1"]}`
- `{"pause": 0.5}` — a short rest after a key point.
- `{"clear": {"keep": ["ax"]}}` — a new page; keep lists what stays.
- `{"quiz": {"question": "...", "choices": ["A", "B"], "correct": 2,
  "right": "the answer AND the reason", "wrong": "a hint, not the answer"}}`
  — optional, near the end, then one short closing `speak` after it.

Rules for commands:
- Put each `speak` ON the command that draws, highlights or animates what it
  talks about. Never two commands with only `speak` in a row.
- Commands name ONLY ids that exist in `elements` (or the template's ids).
- Every element you made should be drawn by some command, in story order.
- Only the fields shown here. Do not invent fields.

## Templates

A template draws an exact figure from a few `params` and names its parts:
`"template": "line_chart", "params": {...}`. Then commands use THE TEMPLATE'S
element ids (given with the template). If a template is given to you, use it
and do not redraw its figure with elements. Leave the template's own `title`
param out; use the `card` instead.
